title: Emergent Properties
definition: Properties that emerge from complex systems, not present in the individual components.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a beehive. Even though each bee is simple, the beehive produces honey, which is a complex outcome.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Emergent properties arise from the interaction of numerous components. The periodic table is an example of an emergent property, arising from the properties of atoms and their arrangement.
difficulty_levels.expert: Emergent properties challenge reductionist approaches in science. They have been studied in fields from physics to biology to sociology. Quantum mechanics, chaotic systems, and self-organization are rich sources of emergent properties. Understanding them requires an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from multiple disciplines.

extra_fields.insight: The periodic table's structure is an emergent property of the underlying components, demonstrating the power of emergent properties in explaining complex systems.
